thread:
alice_customer: hey team — we're seeing a 400 from tool.call when invoking invoice.parse. Error: \"Invalid tool args: Unexpected control character in string at position 58\". Started yesterday after a batch upload. Posting the payload we sent (redacted):

```json
{
  \"tool\": \"invoice.parse\",
  \"args\": {
    \"file_path\": \"C:\\\\Users\\\\alice\\\\invoices\\\\inv123.pdf\",
    \"metadata\": \"copied from windows editor\",
    \"notes\": \"invoice 2026-03-07\"
  }
}
```

alice_customer: we suspect the path copy from Windows might have introduced a literal tab/CRLF in the notes field when we mass-pasted. Client is a small internal Node script using fetch + JSON.stringify.

samira_support: thanks — can you confirm Content-Type header and the SDK version? Also did you observe any escapes in the raw request body?

alice_customer: Content-Type: application/json, SDK: custom node 0.1.2, raw request body logged to our service shows the file_path with single backslashes (not escaped) and notes that looked like it had an extra linebreak in the middle when displayed in our logs.

samira_support: I ran the payload through our strict validator locally and hit the same error: JSON.parse rejects unescaped control characters. Our validator is intentionally strict (RFC-compliant). Error trace: \"SyntaxError: Unexpected control character in string at position 58\" (parser lib: fast-json-parse).

samira_support: Can you try two quick workarounds so we isolate: 1) escape backslashes in file_path (C:\\\\Users\\\\alice\\\\...); 2) replace literal control chars in notes with \\r\\n and \\t sequences or remove them.

alice_customer: tried escaping backslashes — that fixed the immediate 400, good catch. But we want to understand root cause so our desktop users don't hit this.

dev_jun: digging in. Repro steps: paste Windows path from clipboard into a JSON literal without re-escaping -> node's JSON.stringify will embed the literal backslashes unchanged if you construct the object manually from string input; the problem arises when an intermediate step inserts an actual tab or CRLF character into the notes value (for example some editors insert a trailing CRLF or a tab on copy). Our server-side AJV schema validator rejects raw control characters.

dev_jun: short-term recommendation: sanitize client input before sending — run replace(/\\r|\\n|\\t/g, (m) => m === '\\t' ? '\\\\t' : m === '\\r' ? '\\\\r' : '\\\\n') or call JSON.stringify on the string values and strip unescaped control chars. Example curl that worked:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/toolcall \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{\"tool\":\"invoice.parse\",\"args\":{\"file_path\":\"C:\\Users\\alice\\invoices\\inv123.pdf\",\"notes\":\"invoice 2026-03-07\"}}'
```

dev_jun: medium-term: we're adding an SDK patch to auto-escape common Windows clipboard artifacts and to surface a clearer error message when control chars are detected (INF-4321). Long-term: consider optional base64 encoding for binary-ish string fields so clients can opt-in.

alice_customer: thanks — will push the client sanitize now. Can you add a server-side hint so the error message suggests escaping backslashes or removing control chars? Our users were confused by the raw \"Unexpected control character\" text.

samira_support: good point. Created INF-4321 and a support note; dev_jun added a small change to the validator to return a 400 with a clarifying message: \"Malformed tool args: unescaped control character in string. Try escaping backslashes (\\\\) or removing literal tabs/newlines in string fields. See INF-4321.\". Patch queued for preprod. infra-bot: deployed sanitizer to preprod at 2026-03-10T08:30Z.

infra-bot: preprod deployment succeeded (sanitizer + improved error message).

alice_customer: confirmed client patch + escaping worked for our uploads, no more 400s. Thanks for fast turnaround!

samira_support: :white_check_mark: closing this thread — created follow-up to add a KB article under docs about Windows clipboard pitfalls and recommended client-side escapes.
